nodes.title: rc3 adopter feedback: install safety, multi-harness reviewers and parallel-grind friction

acceptance: The 'Install a release candidate (TestPyPI)' section moves to docs/install-release-candidates.md; docs/install-and-usage.md keeps a two-line pointer with the same anchor text and stays within 400 lines, and every link to the old anchor (docs/upgrading.md, docs/release-runbook.md) points at the new file

The new doc shows installing an RC with an extra ([gui] as the example) for pip, pipx and uv tool from the sha256-checked wheel, and the direct-wheel-URL form ("specy-road[gui] @ https://test-files.pythonhosted.org/.../specy_road-<ver>-py3-none-any.whl") for uv tool and pipx, with how its sha256 is checked; it says that uv tool keeps a URL in its receipt, unlike a local wheel path that later disappears

It states that TestPyPI is never an index for extras or dependencies, in any form (--index-url, --extra-index-url, uv --index or --extra-index-url, any index strategy such as unsafe-best-match or first-index), because a squatted dependency name there can outrank PyPI and its setup.py runs; it names no third-party package or uploader

The extras list in install docs names every key of [project.optional-dependencies] in pyproject.toml except dev (today [gui] is missing); a test reads pyproject.toml and fails when an extra is not named in docs/install-and-usage.md or docs/install-release-candidates.md

docs/release-runbook.md A.3 step 5 (Announce the RC) says the announcement carries the filled-in pip, pipx and uv tool commands, with [gui], and the wheel's direct URL and sha256; the human publishing the release posts them. release-runbook.md stays within its 900-line override by rewording, not adding net lines. Out of scope: an rc-install-command CLI command, and changing what CI publishes
nodes.title: RC install docs cover extras and the direct wheel URL, and each RC announcement carries the filled-in command

acceptance: specy_road/reviewer_auth.py decides a claude-code reviewer's launch mode once, for both review delegate and prompt --channel cli: bare only when the reviewer's environment has ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or the user settings bare mode reads define apiKeyHelper; otherwise explicit mode (--setting-sources user and --strict-mcp-config with no --mcp-config, so no repository hooks, project settings or MCP servers load) which reads the subscription login; the RUN record and the filed REVIEW carry the mode used (bare or explicit)

Explicit mode keeps M8.3's reviewer restrictions (the --disallowedTools list, the structured-output schema, the hand-off --add-dir); a test asserts the argv for each mode, that explicit argv never contains --bare, and that bare is never chosen without a key or apiKeyHelper. The key's value is never printed or logged

When a roster entry or flag forces bare and no key is available, review delegate and prompt --channel cli refuse before launching (no RUN record is opened, exit 1) and name the fixes: export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, configure apiKeyHelper, or let specy-road choose explicit mode; orchestrate plan prints one 'reviewer auth:' notice per such claude-code reviewer entry instead of staffing it silently

The note about bare mode and subscription logins is printed by review delegate as well as prompt, and docs say next to billing_route that a claude_subscription reviewer runs in explicit mode and when channels.cli is still needed. Out of scope: a network authentication probe, and other harnesses' login checks
nodes.title: A Claude Code reviewer works on a subscription login: bare only with an API key, explicit mode otherwise, checked before launch

acceptance: specy-road prompt --channel cli writes the prompt and prints the command it would run, and starts no process unless --run is given, for every role (executor, reviewer, rca); --help for --channel and --run says which one launches; a test asserts no subprocess starts without --run; CHANGELOG.md names the behaviour change

A reviewer --run builds its command from the roster entry: a claude-code, codex or cursor entry without channels.cli uses its adapter's read-only reviewer command (M8.3) with the entry's model; it never falls back to the profile's access.cli example; a model that resolves to no API id (unknown) and a custom reviewer command containing --force, --yolo or --dangerously-skip-permissions are refused before launch with the reason

A reviewer --run runs in the leaf's own worktree (the worktree that has the claimed branch checked out), never in a checkout on the integration branch; with no such worktree it refuses and names `--worktree PATH` or the pickup/worktree command that creates one; a test runs it from the main checkout and asserts the launch cwd

specy_road/review_model_check.py compares the model the harness reported (the init or result event's model, as worker usage already parses it) with the roster entry's model after normalising case, separators and display names; a filed record carries harness_model, and on a real mismatch it carries model_mismatch and the gate (review_gate.py) excludes it and review_eligible.py reports it with reason 'harness ran a different model'; an unreported model is a warning only; tests cover match, display-name match, mismatch and unreported
Out of scope: the paste and subagent channels, review delegate's launch path (it already uses the roster entry and worktree) beyond sharing review_model_check
nodes.title: prompt --channel cli launches nothing without --run, and a run uses the rostered model in the leaf's worktree; a model the harness did not report as rostered is flagged

acceptance: specy-road reconcile-branch [<ID>], run in a leaf's worktree on its feature branch, fetches the integration branch, merges it with finish_pr_merge.merge_integration_resolving_bookkeeping (registry.yaml by rule, roadmap.md and roadmap-context.md regenerated with export and digest), commits the merge and pushes the branch when it has an upstream; any conflict outside those three paths aborts the merge, names the paths and exits 1 with the branch unchanged

A test makes two leaves under on_complete: pr, merges the first into the integration branch, then runs reconcile-branch on the second and asserts: no conflict markers, validate, export --check and digest --check pass on the result, and code files are untouched; a second test with a code conflict asserts the refusal and an unchanged HEAD

Pickup's register commit on the integration branch includes the regenerated roadmap-context.md (and roadmap.md when the claim changes it), so digest --check passes on the integration branch and on the new feature branch right after pickup; the commit still changes nothing else (abort-task-pickup's check of its own registration commit accepts those two generated files); do_next_task.py stays within 400 lines by moving the register step to do_next_task_register.py

docs/git-workflow-parallel-prs.md (linked from one line in docs/git-workflow.md, which is near its 400-line cap) and the finish command stub say when to run reconcile-branch (a PR-mode branch whose PR shows bookkeeping conflicts after another leaf merged), and that forge merges do not run custom git merge drivers, which is why the fix is a command, not .gitattributes. Out of scope: a .gitattributes merge driver, and resolving code conflicts
nodes.title: Parallel PR-mode leaves reconcile bookkeeping by rule, and pickup's register commit leaves the digest current

acceptance: When the leaf has an accepted RCA record (RCA-<n>.md accepted under M12.1's next-step rules) newer than its oldest carried blocking review, the ## Rework section starts with that RCA's design and required changes (from specy_road/rework_rca.py), labelled as the governing design, and says that a review's suggested fix contradicting it is overruled; reviews follow it, each marked as filed before or after the RCA

worker delegate --rework's stderr note names the RCA it carries; when an accepted RCA exists that the prompt would not carry (unreadable, or no design section), --rework refuses and names the file instead of sending a prompt without it

A test reproduces the reported case: a blocking review proposing design X, then an accepted RCA choosing design Y; the prompt contains Y before X and the overruling sentence, and a leaf with no RCA gets today's prompt byte for byte. Out of scope: deciding which RCA is accepted (M12.1) and the class audit (M14.11)
nodes.title: The rework prompt carries the accepted root-cause analysis as the governing design, ahead of the reviews' suggested fixes

acceptance: No promote output (sheet, stdout, docs/brainstorming.md, which is at 391 lines: reword, add no net lines) says Approach is filled in at pickup; the promote placeholder under ## Approach (planning_sheet_bootstrap.PROMOTE_PLACEHOLDER; brainstorm_promote.py is at its 400-line cap and must not grow) says pickup skips the leaf until it is written and names specy-road author-approach <ID>; a test asserts the placeholder text and that pickup's skip reason names the same command

specy-road author-approach <ID> [<ID>...] prints, for each leaf whose ## Approach is still a placeholder, the node's title, acceptance, touch zones and ancestor Intent, plus a prompt to write ## Approach (constraints, steps, how to verify) and commit only the sheet; with -o it writes work/prompt-approach-<ID>.md; a leaf with an authored Approach is reported and skipped; it changes no file except with -o

Pickup's guard is unchanged (M3.1: scaffold sheets are still skipped unless --allow-scaffold-planning); orchestrate plan and grind-session --plan list such leaves under one 'needs Approach' line naming author-approach. Out of scope: generating an Approach automatically
nodes.title: A promoted leaf is never stuck: promote's sheet says Approach is written before pickup, and author-approach prints the prompt to write it

acceptance: No adapter puts the prompt text on the command line: cursor's executor, resume and reviewer launches (M8.3's --mode ask included) pass a short instruction naming the prompt file, or stdin, as claude-code's STDIN_INSTRUCTION does; a test for every adapter and every role (executor, reviewer, rca) builds a launch from a 200 KiB prompt and asserts no argv element exceeds 32 KiB

A launch whose argv would still exceed the OS single-argument limit (a custom channels.cli with "<prompt>") is refused before exec with the size and the {prompt} placeholder fix, never as Errno 7 from the harness

specy_road/harness_binary.py resolves the harness binary (claude, agent, codex) before launch: a roster entry's optional harness_bin, else PATH, else the harness's documented install dirs (~/.local/bin for the Cursor agent CLI); not found means a refusal naming the dirs searched and harness_bin, not exit 127; the resolved path is what runs and is recorded. Out of scope: the cursor reviewer's --force (M8.3 already removes it)
nodes.title: Harness launches survive large prompts and a harness binary off PATH, for every role

acceptance: orchestrate plan --roster-from-worktree plans with the working tree's roadmap/orchestration.yaml, prints 'DRY RUN: roster from the working tree, nothing may launch from this plan' first, and its --json carries roster_ref: worktree; worker delegate, review delegate and grind-session never accept it; a test asserts the banner and that delegate still reads the integration-branch roster
models list says which roster it read (the ref) and, when the working tree's roster differs, prints the added, removed and changed entry ids (and changed fields) as 'uncommitted roster changes'

The gitignored roadmap/orchestration.local.yaml may add roster entries under roster_add for this clone (availability overlays stay as they are); planning and delegation on this clone use them, labelled local in orchestrate plan; an added entry never overrides a committed id, and its access.cli or channels.cli is refused unless the clone sets allow_local_cli: true in the same file; tests cover add, id clash and the cli refusal. Out of scope: sharing local entries between clones
nodes.title: Try a roster before it lands: a dry-run plan from the working tree and local roster entries, and models list shows the uncommitted roster diff

acceptance: specy-road models roster --executor <profile-id> --reviewer <profile-id> [...] prints (or with --write adds to roadmap/orchestration.yaml) roster entries with id, family, profile, harness and roles filled from the shipped profiles, in the exact profile: form validate accepts; an unknown profile id is refused with the nearest ids; a test round-trips its output through validate

validate resolves every roster profile: value against model-profiles/ locally (new roster_profile_check.py; validate_roadmap_checks.py, at 399 lines, changes only a call line) and prints the accepted form for a malformed one (e.g. a family/id string); orchestrate plan then reports an entry dropped for an invalid profile as 'invalid profile: <value>, accepted form <form>' and suppresses the 'no eligible executor ... may_process' hint that only follows from that drop; tests for both

Roster ids in the starter orchestration.yaml and in docs/orchestration*.md match the shipped profile ids (claude-opus-5-5, not claude-opus-5.5); a test fails when a docs or starter roster example names an id with no shipped profile or alias

orchestrate plan prints 'coordinator: this session' when no coordinator is rostered and documents how to roster a model coordinator; orchestrate plan --spread assigns executors round-robin among the capable, available entries instead of always the cheapest, deterministically by leaf order; a test pins the assignment for three leaves and two capable entries. orchestrate_plan.py stays within 400 lines by moving assignment to orchestrate_assign.py. Out of scope: cost-weighted or load-aware assignment
nodes.title: A working roster in one command, profile values validated locally, consistent ids in docs, and plans that can spread executors

acceptance: Overlap between ready leaves ignores a configured set of shared zones (default: planning/ and shared/ as directory zones; a project changes it with grind.shared_zones in roadmap/git-workflow.yaml or the orchestration policy, schema-checked) when the leaves' other zones are disjoint; two leaves both naming the same file under a shared zone still overlap

A test with 30 ready leaves that each list planning/ and shared/ plus disjoint code zones yields parallel batches limited only by the batch size, and one with two leaves naming the same planning sheet keeps them apart; the registry overlap warning in validate applies the same rule
grind-session --plan output names the shared zones it ignored once. docs/grind-session.md stays within its 500-line override. Out of scope: merging edits to the same file
nodes.title: Shared documentation zones do not serialize grind-session batches

acceptance: worker sync --wait --until completion|error|intervention (comma list; default any, as today) returns only on those event types, keeping --timeout (worker_state.wait_for_event gains a type filter; worker_state.py is at 389 lines, so a helper goes in worker_cli_sync.py); a test with output events then a completion event asserts it returns on the completion. worker_cli.py stays within 400 lines by moving sync to worker_cli_sync.py
Sync output collapses consecutive output events with no text beyond '(tool use)' into one line '#5-#10 output: 6 tool uses' per worker; --verbose shows each; a test pins the collapsed line
worker delegate --rework treats a completed (finished, not running) worker as ended and proceeds, naming it in its note; only a running or resumable-in-progress worker refuses

When a completion event says the READY file is missing for the new HEAD, the event line offers `worker resume <W> --ready-only`, which resumes the session with a short prompt to write READY for that commit and nothing else; a test asserts the prompt text
Pickup's five-line grind-session hint prints once per checkout (a marker under .specyrd/cache/) instead of on every pickup. Out of scope: changing what events workers emit
nodes.title: Worker loop friction: sync waits for the events that matter, tool-use noise collapses, rework after a completed worker, a READY-only resume, a quieter pickup

acceptance: upgrade's shipped-docs step also adds, when missing and never overwriting, every work/*.template.md that a role prompt, the executor prompt or a command stub references (at least review-record.template.md, implementation-summary.template.md, handoff-ready.template.md); the set is computed from the templates directory and checked by a test that greps the prompt builders for referenced template names

The .specyrd README's 'Updating after pip install -U' paragraph lists upgrade's steps as --help lists them (refresh-schemas, refresh-profiles, shipped docs and templates, refresh-stubs, validate and digest --check); a test compares the README's step names with upgrade.py's docstring list
upgrade --dry-run lists the templates it would add. Out of scope: updating templates a repo already has
nodes.title: upgrade ships the work/ templates every prompt references, and the .specyrd README matches upgrade's steps

acceptance: review delegate builds the packet (review-packet for the commit under review) when it is missing or was built for another commit, prints its path and size in bytes, and proceeds; review_delegate.py stays within 400 lines by putting this in review_delegate_packet.py; a test starts with no packet

The 'named in the packet but not at commit' warning skips paths git ignores (git check-ignore) and planning-sheet globs that match no file, printing one summary count instead; a test with an ignored build path asserts no warning
The packet's 'new suppressions' line numbers are the lines in the file at the commit under review; a test with a suppression added after unrelated edits pins the numbers

When review record refuses an approve over the 'not a defect because' rule, it prints each offending line (number and text) and the rule in one sentence; tests for a two-clause line and a missing-marker line

review list (rendered in review_cli.py, 387 lines, so the marking lives in review_run_status.py) and handoff status mark a failed or incomplete RUN-<model> record as superseded when a valid REVIEW-<model> was filed later at the same commit by any route, as stale-commit records are marked. Out of scope: changing the explanation rule beyond the quoted-span exception in A6

The approve rule's refusal for a line that joins two observations names the joining word and quotes both parts (the trigger is _second_observation in review_record_rules.py, which splits on ' and ' and similar conjunctions); conjunctions inside double-quoted, single-quoted or backtick spans are not split points, as code spans are already skipped; tests: a one-observation line whose ' and ' sits inside quotes or backticks is accepted, the reported shape ('not a defect because base and HEAD ...') is accepted or refused with the word and both parts named, and a line joining two independent observations with ' and ' is still refused
nodes.title: Review friction: delegate builds a missing packet, the packet skips ignored evidence and numbers suppressions correctly, refusals quote the line, and superseded failed runs say so

acceptance: edit-node accepts planned_test_changes with --set, --add and --remove like the other list fields (validated against the schema's item shape), and add-node takes --planned-test-change; a test edits it on a claimed leaf and validate passes

When integrity reports a removed or weakened test not listed in planned_test_changes, review-packet puts it under a 'Required check: unplanned test removal' heading and the reviewer prompt requires an acceptance entry for it, even with policy.integrity_gate off; an approve that omits it is refused by review record with the test name; tests for listed (no heading) and unlisted removals

docs/acceptance-evidence.md says how to authorize a test change after pickup (edit-node on the integration branch, or on the leaf branch where it is reviewed with the diff). integrity.py and roadmap_edit_fields.py stay within 400 lines (the cross-check goes in integrity_removals.py, the field handling in roadmap_edit_list_fields.py; review_packet.py, at its cap, gets the heading from review_packet_observed.py). Out of scope: turning integrity_gate on by default
nodes.title: planned_test_changes can be edited after pickup, and an unplanned test removal is a required reviewer check

acceptance: Model comparison for usage normalises case, spaces, dots and hyphens and also compares against the roster entry's harness_model and the profile's model and display names (specy_road/model_names.py), so 'Grok 4.6 High' matches a cursor-grok-4.6-high slug; a naming-only difference prints no 'model mismatch' and still estimates cost from the roster price

A real mismatch still prints the warning and leaves cost '?'; tests pin both cases with captured cursor stream-json lines. worker_adapter_parsers.py stays within 400 lines. Out of scope: reasoning-token counts the harness does not report
nodes.title: Cursor worker cost is estimated when the harness reports a display name for the rostered model

acceptance: When SPECY_ROAD_REPO_ROOT names a checkout and the current directory is inside a linked worktree of the same repository, commands use the enclosing worktree and print nothing; inside a different repository they keep today's behaviour; worker delegate sets SPECY_ROAD_REPO_ROOT to the worker's worktree in its environment; a test runs ready in a linked worktree with the variable set to the main checkout

env_setup can declare symlinks (link: [node_modules, .venv]) from the main checkout into a new worktree; specy-road adds those names to the worktree's .git/info/exclude so a directory-only ignore pattern (node_modules/) does not leave them untracked, and worker delegate's clean-tree check ignores them; a test with a directory-only pattern asserts a clean status
docs/orchestration-worktrees.md says where env_setup lives and show both the command and link forms. Out of scope: copying environments
nodes.title: Linked worktrees: commands resolve the enclosing worktree, and env_setup handles symlinked environments

acceptance: decisions add --local writes the gitignored roadmap/decisions.local.yaml, which readers merge over roadmap/decisions.yaml for this clone (local wins, listed as local); decisions list shows the source; a test covers merge and precedence
pr_body_footer in roadmap/git-workflow.yaml (string, schema-checked) is appended to finish-this-task's PR body; absent means today's body

implementation_summary: commit | local in git-workflow.yaml decides whether the executor prompt says to commit work/implementation-summary-<ID>.md (commit, the default) or to leave it uncommitted for the review packet to read from the worktree (local); the prompt never tells workers to git add -f an ignored path, and with commit plus a .gitignore that ignores the file, validate says which rule wins

on_complete merge honours land: push | local for the root repository as M14.4.1 does for nested repos: local merges into the local integration branch and pushes nothing, saying so; tests for each. Out of scope: changing the defaults
nodes.title: Project preferences the workflow respects: local decisions, a PR body footer, the summary commit rule, and local landing for the root repository

acceptance: run_check moves from review_gate_ready.py to new specy_road/ready_run_checks.py (review_gate_ready.py imports it); a --run that exits 0 but whose recorded tail has a line containing one of 'cannot open', 'command not found', 'No such file or directory' or 'Permission denied' (case-sensitive, one constant in that module) gets warning: '<that line>' on its verify row; ready prints the warning on stderr and still writes the READY

The review packet shows that warning in bold under the verifier's heading (review_packet.py, 392 lines, grows by at most two lines in _ready_verify); a test reproduces the reported shape (a loop whose earlier step fails with "cannot open" and whose last step succeeds, so the exit is 0) and asserts the warning in the READY and the packet, and a clean run carries none

ready --run-argv '<JSON array of strings>' (repeatable) runs that argv without a shell, records cmd as shlex.join(argv), and is otherwise a --run (same refusal on a non-zero exit, same warning); a value that is not a non-empty JSON array of strings is refused before anything runs; a test passes an argument containing $f and spaces and asserts the program receives it unexpanded. Out of scope: refusing on a marker (it is a warning), scanning beyond the recorded tail, --verify CMD=EXIT rows (they have no output), and markers beyond the four listed
nodes.title: ready does not record false evidence: a passing run whose output shows a failed command is flagged, and --run-argv runs a command without a shell

acceptance: policy.max_workers counts only live workers: states starting, running, idle and paused_by_limit (a session that can still be resumed); completed, failed and terminated records never take a slot, whatever their leaf's state (worker_orphans.holding_slots and _slot_or_existing in worker_ops_slots.py); the refusal's breakdown lists only counted workers; tests: 19 completed or failed records plus one running worker with max_workers 2 leave a slot free, and two running workers refuse

New specy_road/orphaned_claims.py lists every registry claim with no live worker (as above) on its leaf, no live session on its branch (session_presence.list_sessions), and no valid READY at its branch tip, each with its age (from the branch's last commit, else the registry row's started date) and the commands that resolve it: specy-road worker delegate <ID> to resume work, or specy-road abort-task-pickup to release it; handoff status prints the list (review_cli.py, 400 lines, does not grow: an existing line is folded) and doctor prints it as a report-only section that --fix never acts on; tests: a claim with a failed worker and no READY is listed, and claims with a running worker, a live session or a READY at the tip are not

When worker delegate fails after the leaf is claimed (a slot refusal, a usage limit, a launch error), its error ends with '<ID> stays claimed with no worker: retry `specy-road worker delegate <ID>` or release it with `specy-road abort-task-pickup`' (worker_cli.py, 397 lines, changes one existing line); grind-session's hook_failed line for phase implement (grind_session_events.py, today 'phase=implement node=<ID> rc=<n>') adds that the leaf stays claimed and the same two commands, pinned by a test; the orchestrate command's delegate step (specyrd-orchestrate.md) says to resolve such a claim before the next pickup. Out of scope: rolling back the claim or removing the worktree automatically, and claims held by another clone (doctor's registry section covers rows with no branch)
nodes.title: A claim left with no worker is never silent: finished workers free their max_workers slot, handoff status and doctor list orphaned claims, and a failed delegate says how to resolve its claim

acceptance: A sanitized fixture under tests/fixtures/ holds a real long Cursor stream-json turn from this toolkit's own grind (only type, subtype, session_id and usage fields kept; no prompt or content text); the implementation summary states which line types carry usage, as observed. Planner finding 2026-11-05: in real composer-2.5 logs only the type=result line carries usage, once per turn (10 results, 10 usage-bearing lines in one worker log), so there are no intermediate segments to sum

The cursor adapter takes a turn's usage from its result line as today; if a turn ever has more than one usage-bearing line, the adapter sums them and the summary says so; a test with the real fixture pins today's single-result numbers. The undercount is surfaced by A3's plausibility mark rather than corrected (planner 2026-11-05, from the real-log finding)

worker usage (and --json, as possible_undercount: true) marks a turn as 'possible undercount' when it lasted 20 minutes or more (from its start event to its usage event) and reported fewer than 300 output tokens per minute, both constants in new specy_road/worker_usage_plausibility.py; tests: the reported shape (6,092 s, 10,136 output tokens) is marked and a 5-minute turn with 17,000 is not. Out of scope: other harnesses' parsers, diff size as a signal, and correcting the recorded cost
nodes.title: worker usage counts every usage-bearing event of a long Cursor turn and marks a turn whose output tokens are implausibly low for its length

acceptance: review delegate tells the harness the model as worker delegate and docs/orchestration-models.md say: the entry's harness_model, else the profile's id, else the roster id when the entry has no profile (review_delegate._Harness no longer calls harness_model(entry, '') for a missing profile); a test with a claude-code entry with no profile and no harness_model asserts the roster id is the launch's model argument

When the model still resolves to none (a profile whose api_id is unknown and no harness_model) and the entry does not declare routing: dynamic, review delegate refuses before launch (no RUN record is opened, exit 1) with '<id>: no model would be passed to <harness>, so it would run its own default model; set harness_model on the roster entry, or routing: dynamic to accept the harness's choice'; tests for the refusal and for a routing: dynamic entry that launches

review delegate reads the model the harness reported (review_model_check.reported_model over the last attempt's text, M15.3) and passes check()'s result to file_review as prompt --channel cli --run does, so a delegated record carries harness_model and, on a mismatch, model_mismatch, which the gate excludes; RUN-<model>.json gains requested_model (the id passed, or null) and reported_model (or null); a fake-harness test reporting another model asserts model_mismatch on the record and that review list reports 'harness ran a different model'

entry_routing returns dynamic for an entry on any harness whose resolved model is none (today only cursor), and routing_problem's message for such an entry says no model was passed and names harness_model before pinned: true; a test with a claude-code entry whose profile api_id is unknown. Out of scope: worker delegate (executor) launches, the paste and subagent channels, and a harness that reports no model (M15.3's warning stays)
nodes.title: A delegated reviewer always runs a named model: review delegate passes the roster id as worker delegate does, refuses a reviewer with no model, and files the model the harness reported

acceptance: file_limits_engine.SESSION_ARTIFACT_GLOBS includes work/done/implementation-summary-*.md (the path finish_work_artifacts.archived_implementation_summary_rel writes), so an archived summary is excluded like work/implementation-summary-*.md

A test runs specy-road file-limits on a project using the template constraints/file-limits.yaml: a 450-line work/done/implementation-summary-M1.md passes, and a 450-line work/done/notes.md in the same project still fails
docs/file-limits.md names archived implementation summaries among the files that are not measured. Out of scope: other files under work/done/, and measuring a destination path before merge
nodes.title: An implementation summary that finish archives to work/done/ is not measured by file-limits, so finish never lands a file-limits failure

acceptance: When review record refuses after the node and model resolve (any later refusal: notes validation, roster role, signing, the approve rules), it writes work/reviews/<NODE_ID>/REJECTED-<model>.md with front matter commit and refused_at and the refusal message as the body (new specy_road/review_rejected.py; review_cli.py stays within 400 lines); a successful review record for that model deletes it; review_files never reads it as a record (its name does not match REVIEW-*.md), pinned by a test

review list and handoff status (text and --json) show, for a model with a REJECTED-<model>.md at the commit under review and no REVIEW-<model> filed at that commit, 'record refused <age> ago: <first line of the refusal>' (JSON key refused with age and reason), through review_run_status.py; a marker at another commit is not shown

Because review delegate and prompt --channel cli --run file through review record (review_record_write._review_record), their refusals write the same marker; tests: a CLI refusal writes it, a later filing removes it, and a delegated refusal writes it. Out of scope: refusals before the node or model resolve (unknown node, a model not in the roster), and what a reviewer says in chat
nodes.title: A refused review record leaves a trace: review record writes REJECTED-<model>.md, and review list and handoff status show it until a record is filed

acceptance: role_prompt_rca.py holds one TEST_RULES tuple of three sentences: no test imports or patches a _-prefixed name or asserts mock call counts, call order or log text no caller relies on; extend or parametrize an existing test before adding one, and add one only for a distinct regression; never weaken, rewrite or delete a failing behavioural test. executor_preamble carries them under 'Tests:' after its step 3, and the reviewer's excess checklist builds its test bullets from the same strings

A test builds an executor prompt and a reviewer prompt for one leaf and asserts each TEST_RULES sentence appears in both. Out of scope: reading the project's agent rule files at prompt time, and project-specific test rules

acceptance: In review_record_rules._second_observation, a part that _parts joins with ',' or ' and ' counts as a separate observation only when _named_defect finds a defect word in that part. Otherwise it belongs to the same observation. When such a part does name a defect, the first part counts as an observation from two words (today three), so one explanation still cannot cover a second part that names a defect. Parts joined by ';', a sentence end or the other _PARTS conjunctions (' but ', ' while ', ' although ' ...) keep today's rule: a defect word, or three words or more that do not open with a _CONTINUES word

It still refuses 'X fails and Y crashes; not a defect because the fallback handles both.' with 'says "crashes", two observations joined by "and"', and the comma form 'X fails, Y crashes; ...' with 'joined by ","'

Those rows are added to the existing test_clause_problem or test_note_problem parametrize tables, with no new test functions. Every existing row in tests/test_review_record_rules.py passes unchanged except one: 'The cache miss is expected and the cache key ignores the branch name, not a defect because it is handled.' now expects None. acceptance: roadmap_edit_fields defines CODENAME_MAX_CHARS = 64, and every codename derived from a title is capped at that length, including any -<hex> collision suffix. This covers roadmap_crud_prepare.derive_codename_with_collision_suffix, validate_self_heal._derive_codename and maybe_sync_codename_from_title. The cap keeps whole title words, cuts a first word longer than 64 at 64, and never leaves a trailing '-'. title_to_codename's uncapped result stays the same for validate_unique_title_slugs. codename_was_derived accepts both the capped and the uncapped derivation, so an existing long codename still follows title edits

add-node --codename and edit-node --set codename=<value> refuse a value longer than 64 characters with one line, 'error: codename is <n> characters; the limit is 64 (it names feature/rm-<codename> and the planning file)', exit 1 and write nothing. validate does not refuse a node whose codename is already longer, and neither does an edit that does not set codename

planning_artifacts.planning_filename_for_node raises ValueError naming the node when the file name, including the node_key and .md, would be longer than 255 bytes (NAME_MAX), so add-node reports an 'error:' line instead of an OSError. The codename row in docs/roadmap-authoring.md states the 64-character cap

Tests extend the add-node tests in tests/test_roadmap_crud_atomicity.py or tests/test_roadmap_crud_edit_add_remove.py: add-node with a 300-character title and no --codename exits 0, the codename has at most 64 characters and is a word-boundary prefix of the uncapped derivation, and the planning sheet exists with a name of at most 255 bytes. A 65-character --codename is refused and the roadmap files are unchanged. Out of scope: renaming existing long codenames, brainstorm slugify, and branch-name limits beyond the codename

acceptance: AtomicWritePlan.commit in specy_road/bundled_scripts/roadmap_chunk_atomic.py rolls back when write() fails part-way, not only when validate fails. Snapshots are taken before the first byte is written, and any exception from write() or validate restores every staged path (chunks, manifest, planning sheets, staged deletions) byte-for-byte, unlinks each staged path that did not exist before, and removes any .<name>.tmp-* file the plan created. The exception is then re-raised

add-node and edit-node (roadmap_crud_ops.cmd_add and cmd_edit) report an OSError from the write as one 'error: <message>' line and exit 1, with no traceback. write_with_routing and write_node_update give every other caller of the plan (GUI add, brainstorm promote, move and remove paths) the same rollback

Tests in tests/test_roadmap_crud_atomicity.py cover three cases. (a) A plan that stages a chunk and a text file with a 300-character name: commit raises OSError, the chunk's bytes are unchanged and no .tmp- file is left. (b) add-node with planning/ replaced by a regular file: exit 1 with an 'error:' line, and every file under roadmap/ (chunks, manifest, registry) is byte-identical to before. (c) edit-node --set title=... with planning/ read-only, so the sheet rename fails: the same result, with the test skipped when run as root
Out of scope: the self-heal pass that runs before a mutation (heal_before_mutation writes outside the plan by design), git commits, and making scaffold-planning transactional
nodes.title: A roadmap write that fails part-way restores every file it changed

acceptance: finish-this-task writes stdout line-buffered, or flushes stdout before each stderr message, so that when stdout and stderr share one pipe the land check's output comes before the outcome. After a passing land check, the last thing finish prints is either '[ok] merged ...' or one 'error: could not land merge to <ib>: <reason>' line followed by the next command to run

In merge mode (apply_on_complete_mode with on_mode merge, not a rollup), when land_on_integration fails or raises, finish undoes the bookkeeping commit it made in this run. The feature branch goes back to the commit before 'chore(rm-<codename>): complete, deregister' (git reset --keep), and the work files the bookkeeping removed or archived (work/brief-<ID>.md, work/prompt-<ID>.md, work/implementation-summary-<ID>.md) are back at their paths with their original bytes. The error names a plain `specy-road finish-this-task` re-run as the next command. If the undo itself fails, the error says so and names `git reset --keep <sha>`

A branch whose tip is already a bookkeeping commit from an earlier finish still goes through feature_rm_registry to retry_merge_landing as today; its error also prints after all stdout. on_complete auto and pr keep the commit, because the PR needs it. Step 9 of docs/dev-workflow.md and the text of merge_landing_failed describe the new behaviour

Tests run finish-this-task in a sandbox with a bare remote and a passing land check, with stdout and stderr merged into one pipe. (a) A pre-receive hook in the bare remote rejects the push: exit 1, the last 'error:' line comes after the land check output and names the reason ('remote rejected'), the feature branch tip equals its pre-finish sha, the branch's registry still holds the claim, and work/brief-<ID>.md exists. (b) specy_road.finish_modes.land_on_integration is patched to raise OSError: the same guarantees, with the exception text in the error
Out of scope: retrying a transient push failure automatically, the milestone rollup path, and the coordinator scripts under sr/tools
nodes.title: finish-this-task: a failed merge landing reports after the land check output and undoes its bookkeeping commit
